subject: education
intro: Education leads to the classroom and everything that supports it — teaching pupils at every level, guiding their choices, and designing the curriculum and assessments behind instruction.

roles.title: Kindergarten Teachers, Except Special Education
roles.what: Teach academic, social and life skills to kindergarten pupils, planning lessons, managing the classroom and laying the foundations of learning children build on for the rest of school.
roles.where: The Student development unit is the knowledge base for the earliest years, and the motivation and classroom management units supply the everyday skills of keeping young learners engaged and orderly.

roles.title: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
roles.what: Teach academic and social skills to students at the elementary school level, covering several subjects, assessing progress and adapting lessons to the range of learners in the room.
roles.where: The learning process unit explains how pupils actually acquire material, student diversity and special educational needs train the adaptation, and the assessment units are the marking and progress-tracking routine.

roles.title: Education Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in education — often the educational psychology behind how people learn — to university students training to become teachers, sometimes combining teaching with research.
roles.where: This course is the content of the job: the changing teaching profession, student development, motivation, and assessment strategy units are the substance a lecturer passes on to trainee teachers.

roles.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
roles.what: Advise and assist students, providing educational, personal-development and vocational guidance so each learner can choose and reach a path that fits them.
roles.where: Student motivation and development — how learners differ and what drives them — plus the units on special educational needs and communication give counselors the framework for advising each student individually.

roles.title: Instructional Coordinators
roles.what: Develop instructional material, coordinate educational content and bring current technology into teaching, writing the guidelines teachers follow and training and coaching them in new curricula.
roles.where: Planning instruction and facilitating complex thinking is the coordinator's design problem at scale, and the teacher-made and standardized assessment units are the measurement expertise used to judge whether a curriculum works.
